To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a new family of hybrid classifiers that achieve state of the-art accuracy and computational efficiency on the image classification task, and that these models can be thought of either as decision trees with data transformation operators (augmented with a loss function), or as CNNs with sparse weight matrices and explicit data routing.
1) decision forests are CNNs with block-diagonal weights; 2) decision trees are CNNs with data routing functions; 3) conditional networks are decision trees with data transformation functions.

(1) conditional networks are a continuum of hybrid classifiers that combine the best of two worlds, i.e. decision forests and CNNs, (2) conditional networks are more accurate than state of the art decision jungles, and (3) conditional networks can be trained using stochastic gradient descent, with a simple and elegant objective function.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: i) how can we combine decision forests and convolutional networks to obtain a family of hybrid models? ii) what are the tradeoffs between accuracy, efficiency and model size for these hybrid models?
two fundamental questions: i) what is the right model for computer vision? and ii) how to achieve state of theart accuracy with minimal compute cost?
the fundamental question of whether it is possible to achieve state of the ar t accuracy with a fraction (or a small multiple) of the compute cost of a state of the art model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditional computation is an essential component in the design of state of the art image classifiers.
conditional computation can be combined with representation learning to yield models that achieve state of the-art accuracy with a fraction (up to an order of magnitude) of the compute cost.
conditional computation and representation learning can be fused to yield models that achieve state-of-the-art accuracy with a fraction (1/10 to 1/100) of the computation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that decision forests and convolutional networks are two ends of a continuum of hybrid classifiers, and the best classifier is a function of the task and data.
we have discovered a new class of hybrid models that combine the best of both worlds: i) the computational efficiency of decision forests, and ii) the accuracy of convolutional neural networks.
conditional computation and representation learning are complementary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best model for a task may be found somewhere in between the two extremes: decision forests (high efficiency) and CNNs (high accuracy).
conditional networks can achieve a continuum of tradeoffs between the efficiency of decision forests and the accuracy of CNNs.
conditional computation and representation learning are complementary.
